name: Ossuary-Veil

civilization.name: Kirethi Concord
civilization.notes: A starfaring culture that spanned eleven systems before vanishing roughly forty thousand years ago; the Veil ossuary-monoliths are the only structure they are known to have built on this world.

specific_features: Ancient alien ruins: a ring of two hundred basalt monoliths, each carved with spiraling script, enclosing a plain of fused glass
Signal of unknown origin: the monoliths resonate in chorus for ninety seconds at every local dusk, producing a tone with no identifiable source
description: Grey mountains saw against a bruise-colored sky, their flanks streaked with the dust of a thin, tired atmosphere. Between the ranges stretch plains of black glass, smooth as poured ink, where something long ago burned hot enough to fuse the soil. At the heart of the largest glass plain stands a ring of monoliths, each twice the height of a landing shuttle.

The air is thin enough that every breath is rationed labor, and sound dies within arm's reach—footsteps land dull and close. At dusk the temperature drops fast and frost blooms across the monolith script like lichen filmed in fast-forward. When the light fails, the stones begin to sing: one low chord, held for ninety seconds, then gone.

The Kirethi Concord mapped eleven systems and buried their dead on none of them except this one, and no record explains why a civilization of interstellar reach chose an airless valley for its only monument here. The spiraling script has never been translated; every decryption attempt returns the same result—a perfect, meaningless palindrome. Whatever cataclysm vitrified the plain happened after the ring was raised, yet not one of the two hundred stones bears a scorch mark.

Salvage syndicates prize the dark crystals seeded through the glass plains, but extraction crews rotate out faster than any contract clause can explain, citing dreams of standing in the ring at dusk. A xenoarchaeology guild has petitioned for permanent quarantine, arguing the dusk-chord is not residue but ritual—something still being performed. The petition is stalled, the miners keep arriving, and every evening at last light, the Veil sings to both of them exactly the same.
